short: Covariance tangent-space + RVM (M06) is new to imagined-speech EEG but beats only at-chance baselines; evaluation is behind: no test against chance, which 3 of 7 priors ran.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06) to covariance tangent-space features with an RVM [@nguyen2018inferring]. None of the 7 prior imagined-speech EEG decoders used Riemannian features (Appendix), and the gain repeats across 6 to 8 subjects per task, but it is measured against re-implemented baselines at or near chance, with uncorrected tests and per-subject settings chosen on the reported accuracy, so M06 is standard: new to the setting, not shown to beat a working decoder. Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: 3 of 7 priors test accuracy against chance, this paper does not. The authors analyse the window in which the word-specific visual cue is shown, to avoid auditory responses (§4.1); a [later] re-analysis of the released data links the best contrast to muscle tension and that cue and finds vowels and short words near chance once all segments of a trial share a fold [@tates2026unpacking]. The released dataset (Abstract), reused by later decoders [@panachakel2021decoding; @singh2019decoding], is the lasting contribution.
